The given MoA (Mechanism of Action) describes a second-generation peripheral histamine H1 receptor antagonist, which primarily affects peripheral histamine receptors and is designed to block H1 receptors without significant central sedation. This type of drug is generally used to treat conditions such as allergic rhinitis, urticaria, and other histamine-mediated conditions. There is no direct evidence or mechanism that suggests such a drug would cause or contribute to myocardial infarction. Therefore, the plausibility of myocardial infarction as a side effect of this type of medication is LOW.
